claims.text: Conventional high-entropy-alloy microstructures have randomly oriented grains.
Conventional high-entropy-alloy microstructures contain nanoprecipitate distributions that provide robust mechanical properties.
Controlled solidification and thermomechanical processing can directionally align high-conductivity lamellar phases in high-entropy alloys.
Directionally aligned lamellar phases form continuous pathways for heat transfer.
The aligned lamellar phases integrate coherently with existing strengthening nanoprecipitates.
Directional lamellar alignment reduces phonon scattering at internal boundaries.
Reduced phonon scattering through uninterrupted pathways increases thermal conductivity.
The underlying robust microstructure preserves mechanical integrity after directional processing.
Directionally processed samples will have greater thermal conductivity than conventional intermediate-layer samples.
Directional processing will cause no significant loss of mechanical strength.
Randomly oriented conventional microstructures have limited thermal conductivity because of phonon scattering at misaligned interfaces.
The proposed thermal and mechanical benefits will hold in plasma-facing environments at 600–800 degrees Celsius under high thermal and mechanical loads.
The improvement may not persist substantially outside 600–800 degrees Celsius.
The improvement may not transfer to compositions that differ markedly from the baseline alloy.
